articles.title: Nick Kyrgios enters treatment program after accepting one-month ban for cocaine use
articles.summary: Australian free to play again after having suspension reduced. ITIA accepts Kyrgios’s use of cocaine was outside of competition. Fallen Australian tennis star Nick Kyrgios has entered a treatment program after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive to cocaine.
body: After admitting his “huge mistake” when initially suspended for failing a drugs test on June 22 at an ATP 250 tournament in Spain, Kyrgios is allowed to compete again from Friday.
Kyrgios, who had been provisionally suspended since 4 August, had faced a ban ranging from a baseline three-month period to up to four years.

During an interview with International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) investigators, Kyrgios explained his use of cocaine had occurred socially during a night out, days before he was due to play in Mallorca.

The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada)-accredited laboratory, who stated the explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.
points: ITIA accepts Kyrgios’s use of cocaine was outside of competition.
Fallen Australian tennis star Nick Kyrgios has entered a treatment program after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive to cocaine.

articles.title: Australian wildcard Dane Sweeny stuns 14th seed Lorenzo Musetti to reach US Open last 32
articles.summary: Sweeny records biggest win of his career with 3-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-2 victory. But Tristan Schoolkate and Alexei Popyrin fall in second round. Diminutive Dane Sweeny has won a real-life David-versus-Goliath battle to rock the US Open with a stunning second-round upset over dual grand slam semi-finalist…
body: The unheralded Australian wildcard took down the 14th seed 3-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-2 on Thursday (Friday AEST) for the biggest win of his career.
Standing only 5ft 5in (170cm) tall, Sweeny rose to the occasion to reach the third round of a grand slam for the first time and earn a minimum pay day of $US290,000 ($A402,750).
For a couple of heady hours it looked like his underdog countrymen Tristan Schoolkate and Alexei Popyrin would join Sweeny in round three.
But Schoolkate’s inspired run from qualifying finally came to a halt at the hands of fifth-seeded French Open runner-up Flavio Cobilli.

articles.title: Obano to put England career on hold with Pau move
articles.summary: Beno Obano will become the latest England player to put his Test career on ice after agreeing to join French side Pau at the end of the forthcoming season.
body: The 31-year-old loose-head prop won his fifth cap in the defeat by South Africa in July, backing up first-choice Ellis Genge off the bench.
Head coach Steve Borthwick is restricted to a domestic-based talent pool as a key part of the relationship between Prem clubs and the Rugby Football Union over elite players.
England are relatively well stocked at loose-head, with Harlequins' Fin Baxter, Northampton's Emmanuel Iyogun and Sale's Bevan Rodd all younger than Obano and vying for a role.
Sale's versatile 22-year-old Asher Opoku-Fordjour can also pack down on that side of the front row.

articles.title: Daniel Kretinsky to become biggest West Ham shareholder in blow to Amanda Staveley
articles.summary: Royal Mail owner made agreement with David Sullivan. Staveley was pushing to buy stake in the club. Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the biggest shareholder at West Ham after striking an agreement with David Sullivan, dealing a blow to Amanda Staveley’s hopes of buying a stake in the Championship…
body: Staveley was a guest at the London Stadium for West Ham’s 4-2 win over Wolves earlier this week and was pushing to buy Vanessa Gold’s 25.1% stake in the club. The British businesswoman, previously a director at Newcastle, had struck a deal with the Gold family in July and was fronting a consortium looking for a way on to the east London club’s board.

However that arrangement sparked a process allowing West Ham’s other shareholders to exercise their pre-emption rights over the Gold family’s stake before a 5.30pm deadline on Thursday evening. It is believed that Kretinsky, a Czech billionaire and the owner of Royal Mail, and Sullivan have come to an agreement that will see the former increase his 27% stake to 46%. Sources have said there is unlikely to be a way back for Staveley’s group.

Sources have consistently said that Kretinsky, who will surpass Sullivan as the biggest shareholder, is determined to increase his interest in West Ham as they look to rebuild after their relegation from the Premier League last season. His plans were complicated by Staveley entering the picture.

articles.title: ‘It’s huge’: Nike deal breaks new ground in WSL for London City Lionesses
articles.summary: Club owner says deal is largest in women’s game. Claimed to exceed some men’s Premier League shirt deals. The Women’s Super League club London City Lionesses’ new front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike is the largest in the women’s game, according to their American owner, Michele Kang.
body: The length and value of the deal has not been disclosed but sources close to the WSL club are hailing it as a gamechanging moment and Kang claims that it even exceeds some men’s Premier League clubs’ shirt deals.

London City, who host Manchester United on Friday in the opening game of the new WSL campaign, are about to embark on only their second top-flight season, but this summer they have shocked the sport by signing a flurry of some of the biggest names in women’s football, including the former Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas, the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Putellas’ Spain and Barcelona teammate, Mapi León.

It has been reported that the largest current front-of-shirt sponsorship deal for a women’s football team is an approximately $4m per year agreement reached by the new NWSL franchise in Atlanta – who will begin competing in 2028, but Kang told BBC Sport: “I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal. It is higher than the Atlanta number.

articles.title: Bradford beat Castleford to end seven-match losing run
articles.summary: Bradford Bulls end a seven-match losing streak with victory over troubled Castleford Tigers in the struggle to avoid the Super League wooden spoon.
body: Bradford Bulls ended their run of seven straight defeats and deepened the gloom surrounding Castleford Tigers at Odsal Stadium.

The return of three experienced forwards gave Bradford a major boost as they dominated from the start against Castleford, who are without a head coach and have now lost six of their past seven games since beating league leaders Leeds Rhinos in July.

Bottom-of-the-table Bradford took control by half-time with tries from Riley Dean, Connor Wynne, Caleb Aekins, Dan Russell and Waqa Blake as scrum-half Chris Atkin ran the show, while Louis Senior's try was Castleford's only score of the first half.

They improved in the second half with two tries from Krystian Mapapalangi and one from Alex Mellor, but Ebon Scurr's try 12 minutes after the interval was enough to keep Castleford at arm's length and move the Bulls level on points with York Knights, Huddersfield Giants and Hull FC with one game to play.

articles.title: No Britons left in US Open singles as Dart & Jones lose
articles.summary: Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones fall to seeded players as British interest in the US Open singles ends in the second round.
body: Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones both fell to seeded players as British interest in the US Open singles ended in the second round.
Dart said she felt "under the weather" during her 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Marie Bouzkova as temperatures reached around 30C in New York.
Her loss meant Jones was the last Briton standing in either singles draw, and she acquitted herself well before falling 6-4 6-4 to 14th seed and rising American star Iva Jovic.
Nine British players competed in the US Open main draws - the most since 1981 - with four coming through qualifying.

articles.title: Judge makes pivotal ruling in favor of former NFL players attempting to return to college football
articles.summary: The college football season got well underway Thursday night. However, the sports world was also watching closely as the SEC filed a lawsuit against LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin.
body: A crucial decision could determine the fate of dozens of athletes looking to return to college sports. That group includes two former NFL players who are seeking to join LSU after a TRO allowed them to leave professional football and enter the transfer portal.

Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that a federal judge has granted an injunction paving the way for the athletes to return to college football. The ruling will also likely prevent the SEC from imposing sanctions against LSU for adding former professional players to its roster.

“Injunction granted by Judge William Jorden, paving the way for NCAA and SEC eligibility for more than 40 atheltes. That group includes potential LSU transfers Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, setting up a seismic decision for LSU whether they put them on the roster, which is due tomorrow.” Thamel reported on X.

The SEC still has an active lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin, but Thursday’s ruling could significantly weaken the conference’s position. The injunction creates a major obstacle for the SEC if it attempts to punish LSU or other programs for following the court’s order.

articles.title: We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor
articles.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.
body: BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.

However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.
"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.
Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.

articles.title: Louisiana judge rules against NCAA, clearing path for ex-NFL players to join LSU roster
articles.summary: LSU coach Lane Kiffin’s chances of fielding former NFL players improved Thursday night when a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in a high-profile eligibility case.
body: East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden issued his ruling the night before LSU was due to submit its 105-man roster to the Southeastern Conference, which last week announced heavy potential punishment for football and basketball teams that bring in ex-pros.

The ruling clears the way for LSU to list some former NFL players on its roster. How many games they might be eligible to play remains to be seen as the matter continues working its way through the courts.

articles.summary: Five-star point guard Cayden Daughtry, one of the top players in the 2027 class, is taking an official visit to Tennessee this weekend, he told Rivals. The 6-foot rising senior out of Calvary Christian (FL) is ranked as the No.
body: Daughtry’s trip to Knoxville marks his second official visit, as he made a trip to Florida State last weekend. He’s also scheduled to see Iowa, UConn, Florida, Miami, and Arkansas in the coming weeks and months.
In addition to the visits he has set, he’s also considering Kentucky, Michigan, USC, Louisville, Providence, Villanova, and Vanderbilt.

The Fort Lauderdale, Florida native had an historic summer. He won a gold medal with USA Basketball and a Peach Jam championship, earned Peach Jam MVP honors, and put up eye-popping averages: 32.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 6.1 assists per game at Peach Jam.

”I want to prove that small guards are back,” Daughtry told Rivals in a previous interview. “That’s definitely one thing, but another thing is I want to prove is just how much of a dog I am and how much I want to win. I want to show these colleges and NBA scouts that I am here to stay, and I’m not going to flare off, that I’m going to keep getting better every single day.”

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.
body: UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts.

UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters.

FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."
UEFA is trying to oust Mr Infantino from power with a resignation or in the FIFA presidential election in March.

articles.title: NFC South Predictions: Can The Panthers Win The Division Again?
articles.summary: After four years of dominance by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Carolina Panthers surprisingly took the division crown in 2025. Will the Bucs regain it, or will we see another shock in 2026?
body: With Week 1 approaching, the " First Things First " crew of Nick Wright, Chris Broussard and Danny Parkins predicted how the NFC South standings would shake out. And in a division that seems unpredictable entering the year, all three reached a consensus on who they think will finish in first place.
Wright wasn't convinced he would see a leap forward from the Panthers, pointing to quarterback Bryce Young as the reason.
"I don't think there's a lot of evidence that Bryce turned a corner," Wright said. "He had a nice stretch, but overall, the course of the season, it was a hell of a lot like Year 2."
Wright added he expects Carolina to finish at or around six wins.
